text:
marina: Heads-up — after landing the new SM capability detector (device-id flag rework) we're seeing a perf regression on seq128 for the 40B family. Latency p50 +20% and tail jitter up. Can reproduce on our mixed GPU farm (SM86 + SM95 nodes).

aj: ugh. any logs or profiler dumps? quick guess: misrouted kernel path (tensor-core vs scalar) or kv-cache prefetch disabled.

marina: attaching quick grep from runtime logs: 
```
[2026-03-15T10:12:31Z] INFO device-detect: gpu_props->sm=86, tensor_cores=true, bf16=true, fp8=false
[2026-03-15T10:12:31Z] INFO kernel-picker: selected_path=seqlen128_fastpath_tc_bf16
[2026-03-15T10:12:31Z] WARN kv-cache: miss_rate=0.32, eviction_spike=true
[2026-03-15T10:12:31Z] PERF sampling: model=redwood-40b, batch=8, seq=128, latency_p50=188ms, p95=432ms
```
Note: same node with older detector used to pick scalar-prefetch path and had p50=150ms.

ben: I reproduced with a compact harness: docker image redwood/runtime:canary-2026-03-14 and a small script. When we force the fallback order to prefer fp8-disabled scalar kernels, perf goes back to baseline. So it's a kernel pick ordering bug.

runtime-bot: [deploy] Canary rollout redwood/runtime:canary-2026-03-14 -> 12% across staging. Related alert: KERNEL_ROUTE_MISMATCH 8 instances.

devin: For context: the new device-id flag flattens capability bits and we now infer support by 'tensor_cores && bf16'. But some SM95 boxes advertise fp8 hardware support as experimental; our picker is treating any advertised fp8 as definitive, enabling fp8 codepaths that actually degrade qkv layout on seq128.

aj: That matches. Kernel autotuner should gate fp8 path only if (sm >= 90 AND driver_verified_fp8 == true). Right now we don't check driver_verified_fp8.

marina: Proposed quick fix: change ordering in kernel-picker: 1) driver_verified_fp8 check, 2) tf-core/bf16, 3) seqlen heuristics. Also cap batch size for paths where kv-cache miss_rate > 0.2.

sophia: I ran microbench on 3 nodes (SM86, SM92, SM95) with the following command: 
```
python tools/perf_run.py --image redwood/runtime:canary-2026-03-14 --model redwood-40b --seq 128 --batch 8 --runs 30 --collect=kv,latency,route
```
results: SM86 (baseline) p50=149ms, p95=355ms; SM92 p50=155ms p95=370ms; SM95 p50=192ms p95=480ms. KV miss_rate: SM86=0.06 SM92=0.09 SM95=0.31.

devin: wow SM95 is the outlier — likely fp8 path chosen incorrectly there. Can you paste the kernel route heatmap?

sophia: heatmap snippet: 
```
SM86: seqlen128 -> scalar_prefetch (70%), tc_bf16 (30%)
SM92: seqlen128 -> scalar_prefetch (60%), tc_bf16 (40%)
SM95: seqlen128 -> tc_bf16 (92%), tc_fp8 (8%)
```

aj: so SM95 overwhelmingly picks tc_bf16 which is fine, but there's a small tc_fp8 route and that correlates with kv-cache thrash. We need to treat tc_fp8 as experimental until we have validated kernel builds for seq128+kv.

marina: Action items: 
- quick hotfix to kernel-picker to require driver_verified_fp8==true (aj)
- enforce kv miss gating: if miss_rate > 0.2 then lower max_batch to 4 and prefer scalar_prefetch (devin)
- run full microbench across seq in {64,128,256} (sophia)
- add unit test in autotuner to simulate advertised_fp8 but driver_unverified (ben)

ben: I'll open PR for the unit test + picker ordering. small test sketch: 
```
# autotune_test.py
env = DeviceFlags(sm=95, tensor_cores=True, bf16=True, fp8_advertised=True, driver_verified_fp8=False)
assert pick_kernel(env, seq=128, batch=8) in ['scalar_prefetch','tc_bf16']
```

marina: temporary mitigation: pausing canary for nodes with driver_verified_fp8==false. runtime-bot can you pause?

runtime-bot: [action] Canary pause requested by marina. Pausing rollout on nodes: gpu-sm95-*-zone-b.

aj: also let's capture KV cache profiling traces (kv_hits, kv_evictions) at 1s granularity during rollout for next 2 hours. Put results into s3://redwood-perf/alerts/3088881111/ for postmortem.

sophia: started seq sweep jobs. I'll post results once done (expect ~45m). Also adding a quick perf regression alert rule: if p50 increases >15% on stable models with same route, auto-disable fp8 path.

marina: thanks all. This felt subtle — advertised capability != validated capability. We need a small design doc next week to standardize "advertised vs validated" flags and lifecycle (driver probe -> on-disk verified kernels). I'll schedule a 30m sync.

aj: ack. ping me for the doc, I have benchmark plots that show sequence-dependent breakpoints at 96/128/192.

ben: PR inbound in ~2h.

sophia: will upload heatmaps + raw traces to the s3 path aj mentioned.

marina: closing loop: small rollback patch applied to canary (force-disable fp8 path on unverified nodes). Triage continues in thread. :thumbsup:
